newsitem.title: UK: S&P sees no impact on France's SAFR claims rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees no impact on France's SAFR claims rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it was aware of Assurances Generales de France (AGF) and Athena Assurances intentions to dispose of their stake in France's Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR) but said the move would have no impact on SAFR's AA minus claims-paying ability rating at this time.
"SAFR's claims-paying ability rating was determined on a stand-alone basis with no support derived from the ownership structure," S&P said in a statement.

"There is consequently no impact on the current rating. However, should it be acquired by a company enjoying a higher rating, SAFR's claims-paying ability rating would be reviewed for a possible upgrade," S&P said.
S&P AA-minus claims-paying-ability rating of SAFR reflects good management and strong capitalisation together with sound reserving, investments, and operating performance.

Offsetting these strengths, is the fact that the reinsurance sector as a whole faces considerable challenges, with growing competition in most lines and generally softening market terms and that there is a gradual tendency in continental Europe away from proportional to nonproportional reinsurance, which could reduce the stability of certain long-standing cedant relationships, S&P said.
S&P said it would continue to monitor the developments at SAFR.
